# Score import fixtures

These project-authored fixtures describe the same import boundary in the browser and native app. `lead-sheet.musicxml` and its expected JSON exercise D major, 6/8, dotted notes, rests, ties within and across bars, slash chords and chord continuation across bars. `cases.json` also covers legacy JSON, minor keys, malformed input, XML bounds, external entities and unsupported musical content.

MusicXML import accepts one `score-partwise` part with one treble melody voice. Divisions convert exactly to 480 ticks per quarter. Notes and rests use whole through sixteenth durations with at most one dot, octaves 3–6, and alterations -1, 0 or 1. Global standard major/minor keys and supported meters are retained. Missing key/meter defaults to C major/4/4. Chord symbols extend to the next harmony, including following bars; `kind=none` ends that continuation.

Unsupported parts, voices, staves, polyphony, tuplets, grace/cue notes, transposition, changing key/meter, pickups, repeat navigation, unsupported chord degrees/kinds and unsupported notations fail explicitly. Lyrics, visual layout, dynamics and performance metadata are ignored with a preview warning. Compressed `.mxl`, DTD/entity declarations and processing instructions other than the XML declaration are rejected. No external resource is resolved. Files are bounded at 1 MiB UTF-8, XML/JSON nesting at 32 levels and XML markup nodes at 20,000. Both clients require standard JSON syntax and unique object field names, including escaped equivalents (Android's platform JSON parser otherwise accepts several nonstandard extensions).

Specification references checked during implementation: [MusicXML divisions](https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/elements/divisions/), [duration](https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/elements/duration/), [harmony](https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/elements/harmony/), [kind](https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/elements/kind/) and [Android DocumentBuilderFactory](https://developer.android.com/reference/javax/xml/parsers/DocumentBuilderFactory). Android security does not depend on the unsupported `FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING` flag: bounded preflight rejects DTD/entities before parsing and the builder rejects external entity resolution.
